title: UNEP records an Alberta methane leak repaired a week after a MARS detection in April 2026
summary: UNEP records a MARS methane detection in Alberta on April 10, 2026 and repair on April 17. It estimates 175 tonnes emitted and reports ground-camera confirmation that the leak had ceased.
account: UNEP’s original CAN_S_002 case document identifies a methane leak from a failed ball valve connected to pigging equipment in southeastern Alberta. The first satellite detection was on April 10, 2026, and the reported repair was on April 17. UNEP estimates that 175 tonnes escaped. Ground optical gas imaging confirmed that the leak had ceased after repair. The case document was updated on July 1, 2026, and the August MARS snapshot also describes the mitigation. The Chemical Engineer relayed that snapshot on September 4. The operator is not named, and the sources do not isolate the AI contribution from satellite analysis, expert review, notification, and physical repair.
purpose: Satellite-based detection and notification of large methane plumes so that operators mitigate them. This case was that purpose.
system: UNEP IMEO Methane Alert and Response System (MARS), combining satellite analysis, expert notification and operator follow-up; this repair was checked with ground optical gas imaging.
deployer: UNEP International Methane Emissions Observatory (notification); unnamed operators at the Aerial oil and gas field (repair)
location: Aerial oil and gas field, southeastern Alberta, Canada
domain: Climate change mitigation / methane emissions monitoring
segment: Oil and gas production; intergovernmental observatory

ratings.reason: The operator found and fixed a failed valve releasing 175 t of methane a week, within one week of detection. The operator is unnamed, and no cost or further detail is reported.
A single confirmed case among about 43 since 2023, against more than 3,500 alerts. A one-week 4,900 tCO2e release was stopped.

ai_role.statement: UNEP reports that MARS detected the plume and prompted operator action. Its original case document records the repair and ground optical gas imaging confirmation. AI is part of MARS analysis, but its separate contribution to this alert or the repair is not quantified.

fields.account: UNEP’s original CAN_S_002 case document identifies a methane leak from a failed ball valve connected to pigging equipment in southeastern Alberta. The first satellite detection was on April 10, 2026, and the reported repair was on April 17. UNEP estimates that 175 tonnes escaped. Ground optical gas imaging confirmed that the leak had ceased after repair. The case document was updated on July 1, 2026, and the August MARS snapshot also describes the mitigation. The Chemical Engineer relayed that snapshot on September 4. The operator is not named, and the sources do not isolate the AI contribution from satellite analysis, expert review, notification, and physical repair.
